blocks.text:
The programme brings together four very different sides of Brazil. In Rio, you stay opposite Copacabana at Copacabana Palace, go up Sugarloaf and Corcovado, head out to sea towards Ilha Grande, and celebrate New Year on one of the country's best-known beaches. At Iguazu, your hotel stands inside the national park, facing the falls. Bonito replaces the roar of waterfalls with clear rivers, caves and natural pools. The journey then slows down for a beach stay in Porto de Galinhas.

## Hotels along the route

In Rio, the programme includes 4 nights at **Copacabana Palace, A Belmond Hotel**. The One Bedroom Double Suite overlooks the pool, and breakfast is included. The hotel stands directly opposite Copacabana, so you can return to the pool between excursions, then step out onto Avenida Atlântica in the evening for a walk along the ocean.

At Iguazu, you stay at **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas** in a Deluxe room with breakfast. The hotel is inside the national park, facing the waterfalls. Once the park closes, the surroundings become noticeably quieter, and in the morning guests can reach the falls before most visitors arrive.

In Bonito, accommodation is planned at **Arte da Natureza Hotel Bonito**, in a Premium room with breakfast. The hotel is in the town centre. After visits to Rio Sucuri, the Blue Cave and Estancia Mimosa, you can return to town and relax before the next day.

The beach stay is at **Nannai Muro Alto**, in a double bungalow with a sea view and half board. The hotel is right on the beach, and the bungalows have spacious verandas and private pools. Nearby, Muro Alto has a long reef wall and calm water at low tide.

## Highlights of the journey

Four nights at Copacabana Palace let you stay close to the ocean and return to the hotel between excursions. In the morning, the Atlantic brightens outside your window; during the day you can spend time by the pool, and in the evening head out onto Avenida Atlântica for a walk along Copacabana.

New Year in Rio begins long before midnight. More and more people dressed in white gather on the streets beside the ocean, flowers are brought to the water for Yemanjá, and crowds assemble around the concert stages. At midnight, fireworks light up the Atlantic, and the music and celebrations continue into the night.

The ascent of Sugarloaf has two stages. First, the cable car goes up to Urca, then higher towards the panorama of the bay. From the viewing platforms you can see boats, the curve of Botafogo, islands, Copacabana and the statue of Christ on the opposite ridge.

Corcovado reveals another side of Rio. The train passes through Tijuca Forest, with occasional glimpses of the city between the trees. At the top, the statue of Christ the Redeemer stands above a broad view of the coast, Guanabara Bay, Maracanã, the Botanical Garden and the Niterói Bridge.

Ilha Grande is best seen from the water. A private boat travels between green shores, stopping at beaches and bays for swimming. When the engine falls silent, there is the sound of water and birds, and a chance to spot dolphins, sea turtles or large fish.

At Iguazu, you gradually approach the most powerful section of the falls. At first, the cascades are visible in the distance; then the trail opens onto the canyon. At Devil's Throat, the sound of water drowns out voices, spray settles on your clothes and face, and a cloud of mist hangs over the gorge.

Bonito offers a very different way to experience the water. In Rio Sucuri, the current carries you along as you snorkel above the pale riverbed and shoals of fish. At Anhumas, an electric platform lowers visitors into a huge cavern with an underground lake. In the Blue Cave, the water takes on a deep blue colour, while at Estancia Mimosa a forest trail leads to 8 waterfalls and natural pools.

The route ends at Muro Alto, where a long reef wall shelters the water from strong waves. You can swim, ride a jangada to the natural pools, walk along the shore or stay by your own pool at Nannai.
